liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Dark Star** (4 reviews): Reviewer calls it long and lusty, with a hauntingly beautiful transition into Morning Dew, a cello-like string sound leading and Phil close behind; Reviewer treats this Dark Star as the definitive version [7][9][12][13]
- **China Cat Sunflower** (1 review): Reviewer calls this China Cat beautiful [13]
- **Beat It On Down The Line** (1 review): At its very end, Keith picks out a tune from Guys And Dolls just before Tennessee Jed starts [14]
- **Playing In The Band** (1 review): Described as long and spacy [4]
- **Morning Dew** (1 review): Reviewer describes the Dew arrival from Dark Star as slithering and beautiful, and the Dew itself as a monster [7]
- **Sing Me Back Home** (1 review): Reviewer says it is well done [10]

## The recordings

- **gd72-08-24.sbd.miller.18093.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 23 songs; 201 min; rated 4.53/5 by 30 [1]
- **gd1972-08-24.156469.sbd.anon.gems.flac16**: soundboard; 24 songs; 203 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [2]. Said about its sound: Restoration was done on the start of Sing Me Back Home, which has issues in all circulating sources; some tuning came from source 18093 [2]
- **gd1972-08-24.sbd.unknown.151.shnf**: soundboard; 23 songs; 186 min; rated 3.5/5 by 2 [3]. Said about its sound: Slight digital noise over the first line of Sing Me Back Home [3]

## Around the show

- Third of four Berkeley nights; reviewer notes Jerry had brought Bird Song back a few weeks earlier [4]
- Reviewer says this show displaces 8/21 in their top ten, part of a climb peaking at Veneta on 8/27 [4]
- Reviewer thinks it is overlooked because the Oregon show came a few days later, calling the band in peak form [5]
- Reviewer ranks the 24th the best of the post-Europe Berkeley run and says 8/27/72 is in a separate class [6]
- Reviewer rates both the 24th and 21st above the 27th, and praises Dark Star into Dew [10]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd72-08-24.sbd.miller.18093.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Soundboard to reel to DAT at 48k, with missing songs patched from a soundboard-reel-cassette-generations-DAT chain, via Charlie Miller [1]
- **gd1972-08-24.156469.sbd.anon.gems.flac16**: transferred by Mastered by Jamie Waddell and  Jim Blackwood Pitch correction by Jason Chastain Listening assistance, track, FLAC, and pack by Steve Gravel; source: Master SBD Reel > DAT from ANON [2]. Also: FLAC from a source aired on Dead Legs on Radio Valenica in March 2022; no extra analog generations in Sugar Magnolia, Greatest Story and Ramble On Rose [2]
- **gd1972-08-24.sbd.unknown.151.shnf**: taped by Unknown; transferred by Unknown; source: SBD > ? [3]. Also: Shns come from CD-Rs burned from the circulating DAT soundboard; nothing else known about its descent [3]

## Art and photos

- Poster by arizjones.blogspot.com: [Grateful Dead, Berkeley Community Theatre, Berkeley, CA. August 1972, three shows. (SBD)](https://arizjones.blogspot.com/2015/10/grateful-dead-berkeley-community.html) [17]
- Fan art by arizjones.blogspot.com: [Grateful Dead, Berkeley Community Theatre, Berkeley, CA. August 1972, three shows. (SBD)](https://arizjones.blogspot.com/2015/10/grateful-dead-berkeley-community.html) [18]
